title: Mondays and Thursdays
hook: the Prophet ﷺ fasted Mondays and Thursdays (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the soul of the fast, and your line: a shield. No shouting, no quarrels; when provoked, I am fasting. Did your shield sentence get used? Day one thousand one hundred eleven.

Ramadan comes once a year. But in some Muslim homes, there's a quieter rhythm that has nothing to do with the moon's big month: an alarm set before dawn on a Sunday night, a glass of water and some dates, and then a regular Monday at work, fasting, without anyone at the next desk knowing. Then the same again on Wednesday night, for Thursday. No holiday. No crowd at iftar. Just a habit with roots in the week of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Today, Mondays and Thursdays.
screen: `AN ALARM ON A SUNDAY NIGHT.` → `A REGULAR MONDAY, FASTING.` → `NO CROWD, NO HOLIDAY.`

segments.voice: First, the practice itself. Reports in the collections describe the Prophet ﷺ making a point of fasting on Mondays and Thursdays. These are voluntary fasts, sunnah, not required. Much of what we learned about the Ramadan fast still shapes them: dawn to sunset, food, drink and intimacy set aside, the shield on the tongue. But nobody owes them. Second, why those two days. In a report in Jami' at-Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ gives a reason: deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and he loved that his deeds be presented while he was fasting. An accounting, twice a week, and wanting to be found in the middle of a good act when it comes. Third, Monday has its own reason. In Sahih Muslim he is asked about fasting on Monday, and he answers: that is the day I was born, and the day revelation came to me. So the fast on Monday is also a kind of remembering, a small anniversary kept every single week. Fourth, the rhythm matters as much as the reason. A yearly fast is a mountain. A weekly one is a path you walk often. Some teachers describe voluntary fasts as a way to keep what Ramadan builds from fading over the year. And if you remember yesterday's word, the shield, a voluntary fast carries it too: a regular Monday where the tongue is guarded and nobody else even knows. The lesson is about scale. Big seasons matter. A weekly fast is something else: small, chosen, and repeated.
screen: `A VOLUNTARY FAST, TWICE A WEEK.` · `DEEDS PRESENTED, WHILE FASTING.` · `MONDAY: BORN, AND REVELATION.` · `A PATH, NOT A MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: The practice: plan one Monday or Thursday. Settle, and breathe. Look ahead to the next Monday or Thursday on your calendar. If you fast, and it's safe for your health, see yourself setting the alarm the night before, eating before dawn, and going through that ordinary day fasting. If you don't fast, choose one small thing to set aside on that day, from dawn to sunset, as a way of marking it: a snack, your phone at lunch, a complaint. Hold the picture of that day. If you pray, you can make it an intention. The bell holds the time.
Mondays and Thursdays. The voluntary weekly fasts the Prophet ﷺ kept: the days deeds are presented, and Monday, the day of his birth and of revelation. Today's word.
Your line: two days a week. Today, put the next Monday or Thursday on your calendar, and decide what you'll set aside. Day one thousand one hundred eleven.

howItsDone: Some Muslims keep voluntary fasts on Mondays and Thursdays through the year, following the Prophet's practice, eating before dawn and breaking the fast at sunset as in Ramadan.

original.note: Arabic: fasting; the same word for Ramadan's fast and for a voluntary weekly one.

trapdoor: what you thought: Muslims fast in Ramadan, and that's it.
what it means: there are voluntary fasts too, like Mondays and Thursdays, kept by choice.
what a scholar hears: Tirmidhi's 'deeds are presented' report, and Sahih Muslim's 'the day I was born' for Monday.

notes: Tirmidhi 747 (deeds presented Monday and Thursday): confirm number and grading.
Muslim 1162 (Monday: the day I was born and revelation came): confirm number; it is within the long report from Abu Qatadah.
'in some Muslim homes' (hook) and 'Some Muslims keep' (howItsDone): confirm.
'Scholars describe voluntary fasts as a way to keep what Ramadan builds ... and to make up for gaps': confirm attribution.
Practice offers a non-food 'set aside' for those who don't fast; it is framed as marking the day, not as a fast.
Original: صَوْم chosen (siyam also common); confirm.
